**Voica v0.9.0 — works where the only way out is a corporate proxy, and stops pretending when there is nothing to transcribe with.**

This release is mostly about networks Voica could not properly work in, and about a handful of
places where the app looked like everything was fine when it was not.

### Working through a proxy

The diagnosis was not what it looked like. Routing always worked — .NET reads the Windows proxy
settings by itself. **Authentication** was what failed: the proxy answered `407`, nobody sent
credentials, and from the outside that read as "the app cannot do proxies".

Voica now authenticates as the user you signed into Windows with, so a domain proxy is answered over
SSO. **No password is typed into the app and none is stored by it.** The setting covers everything
Voica does over the network at once: recognition, the model download, update checks.

If the proxy refuses, the message **names its address** — that is the thing to hand to whoever
administers the network.

### The Network tab

A sixth Settings tab, before About: the "Use the system proxy" switch (on by default) and a line
saying which route requests actually take — the system proxy, one set for this run, or straight out.

Turning it off is a real need too: a proxy left misconfigured in Windows blocks the app just as
effectively as a missing one.

### The local model: cancel it, verify it, carry it in by hand

- The 215 MB download can be **cancelled**, and nothing half-downloaded is left on disk.
- **Deleting the model asks first**, saying how much is freed and what stops working.
- The model can be **brought in on a USB stick** when a network will not pass that much: file names,
  sizes and SHA-256 are in the README. Voica checks them itself the first time it loads a model it
  did not download, so a truncated copy says so instead of turning into gibberish recognition.
- Choosing "Local (offline)" no longer **starts a download by itself** — behind a closed proxy that
  was an instant failure nobody asked for.

### The app stops going quiet

- **A dictation nothing can transcribe is refused before it is spoken.** With the cloud engine and
  no key, the recording bar used to come up, record for as long as you spoke, and only then mention
  the missing key. The refusal now comes first and leads to where it is fixed.
- **A chosen local engine is never served by the cloud** — not even "while the model downloads".
  "Local (offline)" is a promise about privacy, and breaking it quietly is worse than refusing.
- **Windows and dialogs opened from the tray reach the front.** With no main window, they were not
  granted the foreground: they landed behind the active window and only blinked in the taskbar,
  which reads as "the menu item does nothing".
- Settings opens **directly on the tab you asked for**, without a glimpse of another one, and
  identical warnings no longer stack.
- A failed background update check stays silent and **takes the daily slot**: in a closed network it
  fails at every launch, and retrying helps nobody. A check you asked for still shows its error.

### Install

Windows 10 1809+ / x64:

| File | Size | Needs |
|---|---|---|
| **`Voica-Setup-0.9.0.exe`** | ~75 MB | nothing — recommended |
| `Voica.exe` | ~80 MB | nothing — single file, no installation |
| `Voica-fx.exe` | ~37 MB | [.NET 8 Desktop Runtime](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet/8.0) installed once |

Installing over an existing copy keeps your history, settings and API key.

Not code-signed yet, so SmartScreen may warn → **More info → Run anyway**
([why, and how to verify](https://github.com/Inhum/voica-win#why-does-windows-warn-about-this-app)).

Full changelog: https://github.com/Inhum/voica-win/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md
